sourcedFrom: BENELLI 828U — USE AND MAINTENANCE — 04-2020 — read from the document's own filename and page furniture (2020)
cleanIntro: The 828U is a break-action over-under with a REMOVABLE TRIGGER GUARD ASSEMBLY, and that is what makes its strip different from most O/Us — and more dangerous to get wrong. ⛔ Benelli's rule is absolute: the STRIKERS MUST STAY COCKED while the trigger guard comes out, so the trigger must not be touched at any point in that sequence. ⚠ And the Sport is the variant with Progressive Balancing and an adjustable trigger POSITION, both of which Benelli documents separately from the rest of the 828U line.

steps.title: ⛔ SAFETY CATCH ENGAGED for the whole job — Benelli's words, not ours
steps.action: Engage the safety and leave it engaged. Benelli states that ALL assembly, disassembly and maintenance operations are carried out with the safety catch engaged — and in the same breath that the safety is a mechanical device that does not replace your responsibility.
steps.prose: A maker who tells you his safety is only a device is telling you where the real one is.
steps.aside: Engage the safety catch (see section “SAFETY CATCH”).
steps.quote: ATTENTION: both the manual and automatic safety catch are mechanical devices and they do not replace the responsibility of the shotgun user. All assembly/disassembly and maintenance operations must be carried out with the SAFETY CATCH ENGAGED. 12
steps.cite: BENELLI 828U — USE AND MAINTENANCE — 04-2020 — read from the document's own filename and page furniture — Safety catch, printed p.42

steps.title: Open it, look in both chambers, and note the RED DOT
steps.action: Rotate the top lever, drop the barrels and visually inspect BOTH bores. ⚠ While it is open, note the barrel selector: this is a single selective trigger and a RED DOT shows which barrel fires first — right for the lower, left for the upper.
steps.prose: Two chambers means two things to look at. The dot tells you which one the trigger is pointed at.
steps.quote: The shotgun is equipped with a “single selective trigger”; the selector position highlights through a RED DOT the first barrel that will fire when pulling the trigger:
steps.cite: BENELLI 828U — USE AND MAINTENANCE — 04-2020 — read from the document's own filename and page furniture — Firing selector, printed p.42

steps.title: Fore-end: press it against the barrels, then the release button
steps.action: Press the fore-end against the barrels and AT THE SAME TIME work the fore-end release button, then rotate it slightly and draw it off the receiver. ⚠ The two actions are simultaneous; pressing the button alone will not free it.
steps.prose: Squeeze first, then press. That order is the whole step.
steps.aside: Slightly rotate and extract the fore-end from the receiver (fig. 25).
steps.quote: Press the fore-end against the barrels and simultaneously activate the release button of the fore-end (fig. 24).
steps.cite: BENELLI 828U — USE AND MAINTENANCE — 04-2020 — read from the document's own filename and page furniture — Shotgun disassembly, step 2, printed p.47

steps.title: ⛔ HOLD THE BARRELS — they will slide off their pins
steps.action: Rotate the top lever to the right and move the barrels downward, HOLDING THEM TIGHTLY — Benelli's own warning is that they will otherwise slide completely off their pins and fall. Then lift them slightly and take them off the receiver.
steps.prose: With the fore-end off there is nothing retaining the barrels but your hand.
steps.caution: Slightly lift the barrels and remove them from the receiver (fig.
steps.aside: Rotate the top lever to the right (fig. 26).
steps.quote: Move the barrels downward, holding them tightly to avoid that they slide out completely from their pins and fall down.
steps.cite: BENELLI 828U — USE AND MAINTENANCE — 04-2020 — read from the document's own filename and page furniture — Shotgun disassembly, step 5, printed p.47

steps.title: ⚠ The firing-pin saving blanks come out
steps.action: If the snap caps Benelli calls “firing pin saving” blank cartridges are still in the chambers, take them out now. ⚠ They are easy to leave in and easy to confuse with live ammunition at the next session.
steps.prose: A blank in a chamber looks exactly like the thing you spent the last three steps making sure was not there.
steps.quote: WARNING: extract the “firing pin saving” blank cartridges, if they are still in.
steps.cite: BENELLI 828U — USE AND MAINTENANCE — 04-2020 — read from the document's own filename and page furniture — Shotgun disassembly, printed p.47

steps.title: ⛔ TRIGGER GUARD — only with the gun apart, and NEVER touch the trigger
steps.action: Two absolute rules before anything moves: the trigger guard comes out ONLY with the shotgun already disassembled, and the STRIKERS MUST REMAIN COCKED, which means not touching the trigger at any point. ⚠ Benelli gives the recovery too: if the trigger IS activated, do not force the guard out — put it back in its seat and re-cock the strikers with the top lever.
steps.prose: The recovery is printed because it happens. Forcing a guard against released strikers is how the receiver gets damaged.
steps.quote: WARNING: For all the following operations, be sure NOT TO ACTIVATE THE TRIGGER. The strikers must remain in cocked position to disassemble the trigger guard. If the trigger is accidentally activated during disassembly, it is recommended not to force the extraction of the trigger guard, but to bring it back into position by inserting it in its seat, and reload again the strikers by using the top lever.
steps.cite: BENELLI 828U — USE AND MAINTENANCE — 04-2020 — read from the document's own filename and page furniture — Trigger guard disassembly, printed p.47
steps.warn:
If the trigger is accidentally activated during disassembly, it is

steps.title: Top lever CLOSED, then the supplied tool — and rotate it only slightly
steps.action: Press the pin on the receiver inward to close the top lever, insert the supplied tool into its hole with the curve of the stem following the rear profile of the trigger plate, and press to release the guard. Then rotate it just enough that its back stands about half a centimetre proud, pull it toward the stock, and lift it out perpendicular to its seat. ⛔ Over-rotating it is the one thing that will stop it coming out at all.
steps.prose: Half a centimetre. Benelli gives the number because more does not help and actively blocks the extraction.
steps.quote: WARNING: An excessive rotation of the trigger guard in the disassembly stage prevents its subsequent extraction from the receiver.
steps.cite: BENELLI 828U — USE AND MAINTENANCE — 04-2020 — read from the document's own filename and page furniture — Trigger guard disassembly, step 4, printed p.48

steps.title: That is the strip — and Benelli stops here
steps.action: Fore-end, barrels, trigger guard, receiver-and-stock. Nothing beyond that is published for the owner. ⚠ Before the gun goes in its case, Benelli wants both strikers let down: pull the trigger on the first barrel, move the selector, pull again.
steps.prose: Letting the strikers down is part of putting it away, not part of taking it apart.
steps.quote: 1) Unload both strikers by activating the trigger of the first barrel.
steps.cite: BENELLI 828U — USE AND MAINTENANCE — 04-2020 — read from the document's own filename and page furniture — Before placing the shotgun into its case, printed p.49

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Chokes stay IN to clean the barrel — and go back FULLY BOTTOMED
deepSteps.action: Benelli's note is explicit: when cleaning a barrel with an internal choke fitted, leave the choke in place, because taking it out lets powder residue foul the threads inside the muzzle. When chokes ARE changed, they screw in clockwise by hand and then tighten with the supplied wrench until fully bottomed.
deepSteps.prose: The opposite of the habit most owners bring from other guns, and the reason is printed.
deepSteps.aside: 8) Manually screw the chokes clockwise and tighten them using the provided wrench until they are fully bottomed into their housings inside the barrels (fig. 36).
deepSteps.quote: NOTE: when cleaning a barrel with an internal choke fitted, leave the choke in place to prevent powder residues from fouling the threads inside the muzzle.
deepSteps.cite: BENELLI 828U — USE AND MAINTENANCE — 04-2020 — read from the document's own filename and page furniture — Maintenance, printed p.50

deepSteps.title: ⚠ An “Ampliator” choke changes the maintenance interval
deepSteps.action: If the gun is running an Ampliator choke, Benelli advises carrying out the whole maintenance sequence after EVERY session, to prevent the clamping its ammunition causes. ⚠ That is a shorter interval than the book's general advice and it is attached to one accessory.
deepSteps.prose: A per-accessory interval is worth knowing before it seizes.
deepSteps.aside: NB: all barrels are internally chromium plated.
deepSteps.quote: WARNING: in case of use of an "Ampliator" choke, it is advisable to carry out the maintenance operations listed above after each hunting session to prevent clamps caused by the ammunition fired.
deepSteps.cite: BENELLI 828U — USE AND MAINTENANCE — 04-2020 — read from the document's own filename and page furniture — Maintenance, printed p.50

deepSteps.title: ⛔ The barrel locking pin holes are where this action fouls
deepSteps.action: Benelli names two places for periodic cleaning and lubrication: the trigger guard assembly, and the HOUSING HOLES OF THE BARREL LOCKING PINS. ⚠ The second is specific to this design and is not somewhere a general clean would take you.
deepSteps.prose: A maker naming a hole by name is a maker telling you where his gun actually gums up.
deepSteps.aside: Thanks to its extreme simplicity and excellent materials, the Benelli over-and-under requires no special maintenance.
deepSteps.quote: 2) Remove by periodical cleaning and lubrication any powder residuals (or foreign matters) from trigger guard assembly and from the housing holes of barrel locking pins (fig. 35).
deepSteps.cite: BENELLI 828U — USE AND MAINTENANCE — 04-2020 — read from the document's own filename and page furniture — Maintenance, printed p.50

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Never a case longer than the chamber
deepSteps.action: Benelli's caution is unqualified and states the stake: serious consequences for both the shotgun and the shooter. ⚠ The gauge and chambering are marked ON THE BARRELS — read those rather than the box. Lead or steel shot are both fine with rolled-turnover or crimped cases.
deepSteps.prose: The chamber length is stamped where it is for exactly this reason.
deepSteps.aside: Shotgun functioning is guaranteed with cartridges featuring rolled turnover or crimped closures, and with lead or steel shot.
deepSteps.quote: Non-compliance to this rule would have serious consequences for both the shotgun and the shooter.
deepSteps.cite: BENELLI 828U — USE AND MAINTENANCE — 04-2020 — read from the document's own filename and page furniture — Choice of ammunition, printed p.44

deepSteps.title: ⚠ Solvent-bearing oils will damage the stock and fore-end
deepSteps.action: Benelli oil for the mechanical parts, and specific products for the wooden, technopolymer or painted stock and fore-end. ⛔ Keep those surfaces away from oils containing solvents or chemicals in general.
deepSteps.prose: The oil that protects the action is the one that lifts a painted fore-end.
deepSteps.quote: Avoid that parts get in contact with oils containing solvents or chemical substances in general, which could alter or damage their surfaces.
deepSteps.cite: BENELLI 828U — USE AND MAINTENANCE — 04-2020 — read from the document's own filename and page furniture — Maintenance, printed p.51

deepSteps.title: ⚠ Check the chokes BEFORE the session, not after
deepSteps.action: Benelli asks for the shotgun to be disassembled before each hunting or shooting session, to confirm the chokes are present, clean, fully tightened and suitable for the ammunition. ⛔ A missing or loose choke is a barrel-damage event, and it is checked at the start.
deepSteps.prose: The one maintenance instruction in this book that belongs to the beginning of a day rather than the end.
deepSteps.quote: Before each hunting or shooting session, disassemble the shotgun and make sure that the chokes are present, clean, fully tightened and suitable for the ammunitions.
deepSteps.cite: BENELLI 828U — USE AND MAINTENANCE — 04-2020 — read from the document's own filename and page furniture — Loading, printed p.43

cleaning.name: BARRELS AND CHAMBERS
tasks: Bores and firing chambers cleaned after use — Benelli's first control
⛔ Internal chokes LEFT IN while cleaning the barrel
⚠ Bores are chromium plated; no abrasive is wanted

cleaning.name: RECEIVER AND TRIGGER GUARD
tasks: Powder residue cleaned from the trigger guard assembly
⛔ And from the HOUSING HOLES OF THE BARREL LOCKING PINS — the place residue actually binds this action
Parts exposed to weather lightly oiled against corrosion

cleaning.name: CHOKES
tasks: Choke housings and barrel threads cleaned with a proper thread tool
Bronze brush and Benelli oil on the choke threads
Chokes screwed back FULLY BOTTOMED with the supplied wrench

reassembly: ⛔ Top lever CLOSED before the trigger guard goes anywhere near its seat.
⚠ If the trigger was activated while the guard was out, the strikers are re-cocked by pushing them inward FIRST.
Trigger guard in perpendicular to its seat, front disconnector into its seat in the receiver — no gap between the guard's front profile and the receiver.
Guard rotated and pressed until it snaps in; its outer profile then sits flush.
Barrels onto the receiver pins, then the fore-end pressed on until it latches.
Chokes checked present, clean and fully tightened before the gun is called ready.
fncheck: With the gun confirmed unloaded, close it and feel the top lever snap home. Work the safety both ways and the barrel selector both ways, watching the RED DOT change sides. ⛔ Check the trigger guard sits FLUSH — Benelli's own test is that there is no gap between its front profile and the receiver, and a guard that is not properly seated is one that was over-rotated going in. ⚠ Then do the thing Benelli asks before every session rather than after: take it apart far enough to confirm the chokes are present, clean, fully tightened and right for the ammunition you are about to shoot.
